author: Fret (Guitar Curriculum Lead), 2026-10-05
not_the_pilot_set: server/data/verified_tabs/pilot_verified_set.json (FLE-103) excludes every song whose material is articulation. This set is chosen for them. Opposite requirements by design — see FLE-103 §6.

frames.fret_origin: capo-relative; the capoed string is fret 0 (FLE-115 §7)

units.bar: PRIMARY. A bar passes only if every `fail`-severity check that applies to it passes. `flag` checks never change a pass/fail. Denominators are always printed.
units.tab: SECONDARY, and CONJUNCTIVE: a tab passes only if its setup matches AND every one of its bars passes. Not an average. A tab with one wrong bar is not fit for a stranger to practise from, which is the question FLE-89's bar actually asks.
units.setup: Its own table, scored per (song x field) over tuning, capo, time_signature, feel, key. Reported separately because these are the cheapest defects to fix and the most expensive to miss — and because FLE-89 already spent a revision on a tuning claim.

three_scores_never_blended: note_exact: bars passing / 48, over the 6 songs with committed notes
constraint: bars passing / 32, over the 4 songs without them
scoring.why_not_one_number: FLE-102's finding was that 62% mechanical and 0% musical were both true of the same corpus, and that a gate built on the first would have passed an invented riff. Blending a note-level diff with a constraint check would rebuild that confusion inside a single percentage. The constraint score is also weaker evidence by construction — it says 'nothing disqualifying was found', not 'this is the song' — and a reader has to be able to see which is which.

severities.fail: Counts against the bar. Recording-free and arithmetic.
severities.flag: Reported, never counted. Used where a correct tab could plausibly trip the check — a chromatic passing tone, a bend-free 8 bars, a legitimately uniform sextuplet run. A flag is a prompt for a human ear, which is the only thing that can settle it.

tolerances.rule: Same pitch classes and same lowest sounding pitch, different string/fret.
An upper voice doubled or dropped by an octave.
The fifth omitted from a 4+-note chord.
tolerances.verdict: PASS. The THIRD omitted is always FAIL — that is T2, the defect in 6 of 10 cached tabs.

tolerances.rule: Altered-dominant family (7b9 / 7#9 / 7#5 / alt) substituted for each other.
tolerances.verdict: PASS. A plain unaltered dominant where an altered one is specified is FAIL.

PASS where the bar sets match=superset_ok; FAIL where it sets match=exact. Stated per bar, never inferred. The two also differ in GRANULARITY: match=exact is scored column by column and the column count must agree, while superset_ok is scored over the whole bar (every reference pitch class present, the reference bass still the bass) because a correct arpeggiation of the same harmony redistributes it across more columns.

tolerances.rule: Durations on a bar with rhythm_scored=false.
tolerances.verdict: UNSCORED. The bar must still sum to its time signature — the meter check is never relaxed.
PASS either way, and only on bar 2.

tolerances.rule: feel. straight where shuffle is specified.
tolerances.verdict: FAIL. swing and shuffle are NOT interchangeable (FLE-115 §2.5). Literal triplet-eighth pairs PLUS feel=shuffle is also FAIL — the swing applied twice.

tolerances.rule: Capo shapes transposed to absolute frets with capo=0 and the right sounding pitches.
tolerances.verdict: FLAG, not FAIL, in its own column. The pitches are right and the fingering is unidiomatic — a pedagogy defect.

tolerances.rule: A different passage of the same song.
tolerances.verdict: NOT SCORED. Reported as passage_mismatch. A diff against the wrong eight bars is noise, not a measurement.

tolerances.rule: A forbidden pitch class appearing only below the stated min_duration.
tolerances.verdict: FLAG. A chromatic passing tone is not FLE-102's T5, which was five bars of structural wrong notes.

tolerances.rule: Column 6 of a House of the Rising Sun bar.
tolerances.verdict: PASS for any note of the declared chord. A genuine arrangement variant.

scoring.what_this_cannot_measure: A well-formed invention. FLE-102's Kashmir passed 8 of 8 mechanical checks and had nothing to do with the song. Against this set that specific invention now fails (pitch_set_not), but the general case does not: a generator that emits a plausible, meter-correct, in-key riff for a song whose notes I did not commit scores well and is still wrong. The 48 note_exact bars are the only part of this set immune to that, and they cover 6 of 10 songs. Do not report the constraint score as accuracy.

songs.title: Sweet Home Chicago
songs.arrangement: The standard band reading: 12-bar in E, shuffle feel, boogie figure on the two lowest strings. NOT Johnson's own 1936 solo performance, which is a fingerpicked country-blues arrangement and a different guitar part. The catalog credits Johnson; the arrangement every blues player means by this title is the electric one, and that is what I committed. Which of the two Fletcher teaches is a curation call for Junie, not a tab question — but the ground truth has to name one, so it names this.
songs.passage: Bars 1-8 of the 12-bar form: I I I I IV IV I I.
songs.why_in_set: The cheapest possible test of the one thing FLE-115 §2.5 added: a tab that gets every fret right and leaves `feel` at `straight` is not this song. FLE-102 also found T10 here — two bars, neither of which added up to 4/4 — so the meter check has a real prior failure to regress against.

song_requirements.why: A Chicago shuffle played straight is a different rhythm. FLE-102: notated straight in the cached tab.
A-9: triplet-eighth pairs PLUS feel:shuffle double-applies the swing. The groove is the mark, not the notation.

requirements.why: The boogie's whole pitch content. A third anywhere here is wrong (this figure has none) and so is a missing b7 — the b7 is what makes it a blues rather than a rock fifth.

songs.title: Comfortably Numb
songs.arrangement: Standard tuning. The first solo, over the verse changes in B minor.
songs.basis_note: CONSTRAINT ONLY. I will not publish a bar-by-bar transcription of this solo from memory — see cannot_verify. What I can certify cold is the whole of the defect FLE-102 measured: every C in the cached tab is C natural where B minor requires C#, five bars of it, which turns B Aeolian into B Phrygian. That is checkable with no recording, it contradicts the breakdown's own chord list, and it is the single most audible wrong note available over Bm.
songs.why_in_set: The bend song. FLE-102: 'bends, sustain, vibrato' is what the song is made of and 'fret numbers' is what the schema could say. FLE-115 §5 fixed that, so a tab of this passage with no `bend` anywhere is now a defect the schema can name, and this is the bar that names it.

song_requirements.why: T5. B natural minor has C#, not C. Qualified by duration on purpose: FLE-102's defect was five bars of STRUCTURAL C naturals. A chromatic passing tone shorter than an eighth is not that defect, so it is reported as a flag instead of a failure (tolerance A-13).
A bend-led melody with no bend in eight bars is not this solo. Threshold at a whole step: Gilmour's phrasing is full-tone and wider, and a 0.5 would pass on an ornament.
Half-or-longer notes, a tie, or let_ring. The cached tab was an even grid of short notes, which is not a sustained melody — and this is now expressible (FLE-115 §4, §6).
FLE-102 named vibrato as load-bearing here. Flag, not fail: a correct 8-bar excerpt could land without one.
B Aeolian. Flag, not fail: Gilmour bends outside the scale and a bent note's sounding pitch is not an integer fret (FLE-115 §5), so a fail here would punish correct phrasing.

cannot_verify.what: The solo note for note, and the exact bend targets.
cannot_verify.need: The record plus a reference transcription. I know this solo as a listener, not as a chart I could publish bar by bar, and writing it from memory would put the same class of error into the ground truth that the ground truth exists to catch.

cannot_verify.what: Whether the verse is Bm-A-G-Em or carries a D substitution.
cannot_verify.need: The record. Not committed, which is why there are no chord bars on this song even though its harmony is the part I am surest of.

songs.title: The House of the Rising Sun
songs.passage: Verse, bars 1-8: Am C D F Am C E E.
songs.why_in_set: Two things nothing else in the set tests. First, a meter that is not 4/4 — `time_signature_beats('6/8')` is 3, and a bar of six eighths is the cheapest way to catch a consumer that assumed four. Second, the mode flip in the direction nobody guards: this is in A minor and contains D MAJOR (F# natural) and E MAJOR (G# natural). A generator that reasons 'A minor, so use the natural minor scale' emits Dm and Em and is wrong on three of eight bars. FLE-102's T1 was always a major third where a minor belonged; Hotel California tests both directions in the pilot set, and this tests the reverse one here.

song_requirements.why: The raised thirds of the D and E chords. Their absence IS the reverse mode flip, and it is arithmetic, not opinion.

cannot_verify.what: The sixth eighth of each bar.
cannot_verify.need: Nothing — it is a genuine arrangement variant. Every published reading ascends through the shape; whether the sixth note steps back down or repeats the top varies. Tolerance A-14 accepts any note of the declared chord in column 6.

songs.title: Kashmir
songs.arrangement: DADGAD. The main riff: a sustained low-D drone under a stepwise ascending line, the guitar figure cycling in 3 against the drums' 4.
songs.basis_note: CONSTRAINT ONLY. FLE-102 already measured why this song matters: the cached tab passes 8 of 8 mechanical checks and is a completely invented riff — a I-IV-V power-chord vamp at frets 0/5/7 where the song has a chromatic ascent. That is the gap between 62% mechanical and 0% musical, in one song. So the ground truth here is aimed squarely at it: the pitch-class SET of that vamp is {D, G, A}, and a bar whose entire content is {D, G, A} is the defect. I can assert that without a transcription.
songs.why_in_set: The DADGAD entry the issue asked for, and the only song in either set whose tuning is not a uniform shift — so `_tuning_offset` returns None and the shape-name frame does not exist. Any consumer that assumes a second frame breaks here.

song_requirements.why: Confirmed in FLE-102 — the one thing the cached tab got right.
T6. A bar sounding exactly and only D/G/A is the invented I-IV-V vamp FLE-102 found substituted for the riff.
The low D pedal is the riff's floor. Expressible now via let_ring / tie / a long duration (FLE-115 §4, §6).
The line climbs by semitones and tones from the tonic. Three consecutive adjacent steps is the weakest assertion that still excludes a fifths-only vamp, and it needs no transcription.
T9. Eight bars of identical uniform quarters is the shape of a fabricated riff, not of this one.

songs.schema_gap: The 3-against-4 cannot be expressed. `time_signature` is per measure and there is one voice, so notating the guitar in 3/4 loses its relationship to the 4/4 bar, and notating it in 4/4 loses the polyrhythm. FLE-115 did not close this and I am not asking it to for v1 — a `voices` layer was already ruled out of scope (FLE-105 Q3). Recorded here so the regression set states its own blind spot rather than scoring around it.

cannot_verify.what: The riff note for note in DADGAD.
cannot_verify.need: The record plus a reference transcription. I know the tuning, the drone, the direction of the line and the polyrhythm; I do not know the fret numbers cold, and FLE-102's own verdict on this song was that a well-formed invention is the worst failure mode we have. I will not add one.

songs.title: Wonderwall
songs.arrangement: Standard tuning, capo at 2. Gallagher's four voicings, with the top two strings held at 3 throughout.
songs.passage: Verse, bars 1-8: Em7 G Dsus4 A7sus4, twice.
songs.why_in_set: FLE-103 §4 found the capo gap and excluded this song rather than work around it; FLE-115 §7 added the field, and this is the bar that holds it to the convention. Three distinct things fail here if the capo is wrong: every sounding pitch is two semitones flat, `Chord.sounding_name` is absent or untransposed, and a drill snippet cut from this tab that takes capo 0 is silently in a different key (§7.1.4 — the defect that section was written for). The committed shapes are capo-RELATIVE: the capoed string is fret 0.

song_requirements.why: Not a label. sounding_pitch = open(tuning) + capo + fret.
FLE-115 §7.2 — with capo > 0 the shape name alone tells the player the wrong key. Em7 here sounds F#m7.

A-11. A tab that emits the right SOUNDING pitches as absolute frets with capo 0 is pitch-correct and hands the player unidiomatic barres instead of these open shapes. A pedagogy defect, not a pitch defect, so it is flagged and reported in its own column rather than failed.

cannot_verify.need: Nothing recording-side — the schema has no strum direction and no way to say 'down-down-up-up-down-up'. Out of scope for v1; the bars are scored on pitch and meter only (A-7).

songs.title: Little Wing
songs.arrangement: Eb tuning, standard shapes, so it sounds a semitone below the names. The chord bed of the intro/verse, without Hendrix's fills.
songs.passage: Intro/verse, bars 1-8: Em G Am Em Bm Bb Am C.
songs.why_in_set: FLE-102's worst tab of ten, and among the newest — 1 of 8 chords right, opening on E major plus a b6 where Em belongs, an 8-bar excerpt using all 12 pitch classes, and a chord list carrying E7#9, which is Purple Haze and not this song. The chord bed is the part of this arrangement I can certify cold and it is also where every one of those defects lives, so the fills being out of scope costs the regression set nothing.

song_requirements.why: T1. In the shape frame G# is the major third of the E tonic; the song is in Em and needs G natural. FLE-102 found it in bars 4 and 7 of the cached tab. Note the frame: in Eb tuning the shape G# sounds G, and both are wrong for the same reason.
T7. The cached 8 bars used all 12. Ten is generous — this progression needs eight — and still catches a chromatic cluster.
T7 per bar. The cached m3 was a five-note stack holding both a minor third and a major seventh. Flag: a legitimate 6-note voicing with a doubled octave can reach 5 distinct classes.
Confirmed against the catalog in FLE-102.

cannot_verify.what: Hendrix's fills, the thumb-over voicings and the slides.
cannot_verify.need: The record plus a reference transcription. The committed bars are the chord bed; `match: exact` is correct for them because a chord stab with an added note is a different voicing, but it means a full transcription with fills will not score against this song. Stated rather than hidden: that is a known limit of this entry.

cannot_verify.what: Whether bar 6 is Bb or Bbmaj7 in the published charts.
cannot_verify.need: Nothing — both spell Bb-D-F plus an optional A. Tolerance A-3 accepts either; the third is what matters.

songs.title: Big Love
songs.arrangement: UNDECIDED, and that is the point — see cannot_verify. Standard tuning, E minor, a fast fingerpicked alternating pattern in both readings.
songs.basis_note: CONSTRAINT ONLY, and for a different reason from the other three. It is not that I cannot hear it — it is that 'correct' is UNDEFINED. FLE-102 flagged this already: the 1987 Tango in the Night studio part and Buckingham's solo live arrangement are different guitar parts, the breakdown names neither, and the song is off-catalog under 'Fleetwood Mac' (FLE-108). Committing one arrangement as ground truth would be answering a product question with a transcription. What survives both readings is what I committed.
songs.why_in_set: The fingerpicked entry the issue asked for, and the one place a real pattern-shaped assertion can be made: an alternating-thumb figure has a moving bass with upper-voice notes BETWEEN the bass notes. 'Undifferentiated notes' (FLE-102's phrase for the cached tab) fails that structurally, with no recording and no arrangement decision needed.

song_requirements.why: T1. FLE-102 found bars 7-8 alternating an E bass with G# — the song is in Em and that G should be natural. True in either arrangement, which is why it is a fail despite the rest being open.
An alternating thumb alternates. One repeated bass note is a pedal, not this pattern.
The defining structure: at least one upper-voice column BETWEEN two bass columns. A tab whose bass notes are all adjacent has the notes and not the pattern.
The figure is a fast picking pattern. Flag not fail: uniform sixteenths are legitimate here, so `not_uniform_duration` would be a false positive — the wrong guard for this song.

cannot_verify.what: WHICH ARRANGEMENT we teach — studio 1987 or Buckingham solo live.
cannot_verify.need: A product decision, from Hernan through Miagi, and then the record. This is not a tab question and I should not settle it by picking one. Until it is settled, no note-exact ground truth for this song can exist, and the four assertions above are the whole of what is scorable.

songs.title: Eruption
songs.arrangement: Eb tuning. The tapped section, plus the A-minor arpeggio figure that precedes it.

setup.key: A minor shapes / Ab minor sounding

songs.basis_note: CONSTRAINT ONLY. Four assertions, every one of which the cached tab failed and none of which needs the record: the section is tapped, it is in sextuplets, it is in A minor, and it is built on pull-offs. FLE-102 found it written as 'eight repeated open high-E eighth notes' for bar 1 and an A MAJOR arpeggio labelled A minor for bars 2-3.
songs.why_in_set: The only entry in either set that exercises `technique: tap` and `triplet-sixteenth`. Both are new in FLE-115 and both were previously inexpressible, which is exactly how 'tapping written as plain eighths' survived to production. A schema field with no regression test is a field the generator will quietly never use.

song_requirements.why: It is the tapped section. Per bar, not per passage: the cached tab would have passed a passage-level check by tapping once.
Sextuplets. FLE-102: written as even eighths.
The tap-pull-pull cell is the mechanic. Now expressible (FLE-115 §4), and the link's direction is checked against the target fret for free.
T1. In the shape frame C# is the major third of A; the figure is A minor and needs C natural. FLE-102 found the arpeggio spelling A-E-A-C#-E-C#-A-E and calling it 'A minor (open)'.
T9. Flag not fail: a sextuplet run IS uniform, legitimately.

cannot_verify.what: The tapped pitches bar by bar.
cannot_verify.need: The record plus a reference transcription.

Nothing actionable. Van Halen I was recorded roughly a quarter-tone flat; Eb is a defensible approximation and FLE-102 did not count it as a defect. The schema can express a 0.25 curl on a note (FLE-115 §5.1) but not a guitar tuned between frets, and it should not try.

songs.title: Sultans of Swing
songs.arrangement: Standard tuning, fingerpicked. The intro's chord bed, without Knopfler's fills.
songs.passage: Intro, bars 1-8: Dm C Bb A, twice.
songs.why_in_set: The trap is bar 4. The progression is Dm-C-Bb-A and that last chord is A MAJOR — the harmonic-minor dominant, which needs C#. A generator that derives the chords from the D natural minor scale emits Am and is wrong on two of eight bars, in the one place a listener notices immediately. This is the Hotel California test (Bm needs D, F#7 needs A#, one bar apart) moved into a song whose changes are not in dispute, and FLE-102's single most common defect was a third in the wrong direction.

song_requirements.why: The raised third of the V. Its absence is the mode flip, and it is arithmetic — no recording needed.
Knopfler's part is fingerpicked with legato fills. Flag: the chord bed alone is a correct, if plain, reading of these 8 bars.
Flag, not fail. The intro's first eight bars can legitimately land without one; this is the second bend-led entry and the failing threshold lives on Comfortably Numb.

cannot_verify.what: Knopfler's arpeggiation figure and fills, note for note.
cannot_verify.need: The record plus a reference transcription. The harmony Dm-C-Bb-A is not in dispute and is what is committed.
